desc:
You are given a string s whose letters can be rearranged into a palindrome. In one move you may swap two adjacent characters. Return the minimum number of moves needed to turn s into some palindrome (any palindrome is acceptable, you choose which one).

For example, "aabb" needs 2 moves (aabb → abab → abba); "abab" needs 1 (abab → abba); "aab" needs 1 (aab → aba); "racecar" needs 0.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
At least one palindrome can be formed by rearranging the letters of s
hints: For a short string you could search over all palindromes you can form and count adjacent swaps for each. That is far too many. Fix the outer pair first.
Look at the first character. Its partner has to end up at the last position; the cheapest partner is the nearest equal character counted from the right end.

Use two pointers l = 0 and r = n - 1. Find the rightmost position k with s[k] == s[l]. If k > l, move it to position r with r - k swaps and shrink both pointers. If k == l the character is the single odd one: swap it one step towards the middle (cost 1) and look again.
editorial: Greedy from the outside in. For the leftmost remaining character c, the right end of the remaining window must hold a partner of c. Choosing the nearest copy of c from the right end uses the fewest swaps to carry it to that end, and it does not disturb the relative order of the other characters, so the choice never hurts later steps. After bringing it, the outer pair is final, and we solve the inside window the same way.

If the search from the right finds only l itself, then c is the letter with odd frequency and belongs to the centre. Rather than carrying it to the middle at once, swap it with its right neighbour (cost 1) and repeat; this moves it gradually towards the centre while the pairs of other letters are handled, and its total cost equals the distance it needs to travel. Each outer step costs O(n) for the search and the move, so the algorithm is O(n2) time, fine for n up to 2,000.
solution:
def minSwapsToPalindrome(s):
    s = list(s)
    l, r = 0, len(s) - 1
    moves = 0
    while l < r:
        k = r
        while k > l and s[k] != s[l]:
            k -= 1
        if k == l:
            s[l], s[l + 1] = s[l + 1], s[l]
            moves += 1
            continue
        ch = s.pop(k)
        s.insert(r, ch)
        moves += r - k
        l += 1
        r -= 1
    return moves
